sources.says: N52: drain plug is behind a small removable access panel on the underside; panel shape and fasteners differ by poster (a triangular panel; three screws); plug orientation reports differ (straight down vs facing right).

E90/E91/E92/E93 DIY: the drain bolt is behind an access hatch just behind the front-centre jack point, opened with a coin; 17 mm socket on a ratchet; copper crush washer replaced each time; the pan is placed a few inches to the right of the bolt.

Create ONE clean, polished, instructional illustration for a DIY car-repair guide. Text-only prompt: do not use, request or trace any reference image.

SUBJECT: Oil drain: where the undertray access hatch is, on a 2010 BMW 328i (E90) with the 3.0L inline-6, shown so a home mechanic can see what the step is about. Step: "Open the undertray access hatch".

FRAMING: Landscape, exactly 16:10 (deliver 1600x1000 px or larger at 16:10). Low view from beneath the front of the car looking rearward, mild perspective. LOCATE image: wide enough that a mechanic can find the part. Show the hero in its simplified surrounding structure, the hero taking roughly 15-30% of the frame width, the surroundings plain and simplified. Style (CG-VS-1.0): clean, realistic 3D technical illustration; light neutral studio background (soft white to light grey); matte materials, soft light, soft contact shadows; tight component framing; minimal unnecessary detail. Realism applies to materials and lighting only: it does NOT license invented detail, so every part not listed below stays a plain generic shape. No orange or other saturated accent colours anywhere (a copper-coloured part may be copper); highlights and arrows are added later as an editable overlay.

1. HERO: A small closed access hatch set into the lower undertray near the front-centre of the underside, drawn as a plain flat panel with a simple outline. Do NOT depict its fine detail, where its fasteners sit: keep it a plain generic shape.

MAY SHOW, SIMPLIFIED AND DIM (background only): undertray panel. Keep every one of these generic and low-contrast. Never invent detail on them.

MUST NOT SHOW (leave these out entirely, do not substitute): front bumper and grille (No source establishes the lower front styling for this car; left out), suspension and subframe (No source establishes the surrounding chassis layout; left out), wrench or socket, hands, people, engine badges, logos, brand marks, licence plates.
